label: Avatar Group
title: Avatar Group
summary: Show several people or identities as one compact visual cue.
corePrinciple: Share one size across the Avatar children.

anatomy.title: Each child keeps its own face in the overlap
anatomy.description: The group layers its child Avatars in order. The last child sits in front, while a cutout keeps the next face visible.
blocks: It starts at the back of the visual order and gives the group its first face.
It overlaps the first child and sits behind the last.
The final child is drawn in front. Child order therefore changes which face leads.

configuration.title: Change the shared size or the child content
configuration.description: Avatar Size belongs to the group mode. The children supply the image or monogram; there is no separate count or gap control.
blocks: The group places each child in order and keeps one shared owner size.
The group mode supplies one size to every child; each Avatar supplies its own image or monogram.

states.title: Content and loading belong to each Avatar
states.description: Avatar Group does not add a selected, disabled, or loading state. A child can be loading while the others remain visible.
blocks: The group stays a compact composition of the children it receives.
The loading child shows a same-size skeleton while the other Avatar children remain visible.

sizing.title: The host needs room for every child
sizing.description: The row grows with its child count. A narrower host does not reduce Avatar Size automatically, so select a supported size that fits.

content.title: Compose the group from Avatar children
content.description: AvatarGroup contains an ordered row of Avatar children. Each child supplies its own image or monogram content.
blocks: The group’s content is the Avatar instances supplied inside it.
Each Avatar can show its own image or monogram.
The last child sits in front in the overlapping group.

inContext.title: Show who can access a shared account
inContext.description: A public Coin Card can wrap its title, support text, and AvatarGroup in one composition. The group itself contains only its Avatar children.
blocks: The Card adds optional context outside the AvatarGroup component.
specimen: People who can view this account

doDont.title: Respect shared size and host width
doDont.description: AvatarGroup derives its members from child Avatars. Its owner mode can size them together, and their count determines the row width.
blocks: All three children inherit M from AvatarGroup.
An explicit L child mode takes precedence over the group’s M mode.
All three circles stay inside the visible 112 px host.
This five-child row extends past both edges, so the host clips its outer Avatars.

blocks: Public component master and exposed properties
Docs page and public example behavior

The declared and installed jfs-components version is 0.1.60; the earlier registry check on 23 September also returned 0.1.60. A fresh registry lookup could not be confirmed during recovery because registry DNS was unavailable. Figma’s Avatar Size mode sets L/M/S/XS to 42/36/29/14 px. The public group derives its count from children and uses token-owned overlap; it exposes no count or gap choice. Storybook’s custom-gap example has no gap control. Keep child sizes aligned with the group owner.
